topic: Typography and Color Theory for Interfaces
learningObjectives: Select typography that supports readability and interface hierarchy.
Apply basic color theory to interface components.
Create accessible and visually consistent text and color combinations.

activities.title: Typography Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the key parts of an interface typography system.

content.concept: A typography system defines font family, size, weight, line height, and hierarchy to create readable and consistent interfaces.
content.tip: Explore each typography property and observe how it affects readability and hierarchy.

descriptions: Defines the visual character and readability of text.
Controls the visual scale of text.
Controls emphasis and distinguishes headings from supporting text.
Controls vertical space between lines of text.
Organizes headings, body text, labels, and supporting information.

activities.title: Type Scale Slider
activities.instruction: Adjust the type scale and observe how hierarchy changes.

content.concept: A consistent type scale creates predictable differences between headings, subheadings, body text, labels, and supporting content.
content.tip: Increase the difference between heading and body sizes until the hierarchy becomes easy to scan.

activities.title: Color Role Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each interface color to its appropriate role.

content.concept: Color roles help communicate actions, states, hierarchy, information, and brand identity consistently.
content.tip: Think about what the user needs to understand before choosing a color role.

choices: Error — Failed actions or critical problems

activities.title: Contrast Checker Lab
activities.instruction: Adjust contrast until the text is clearly readable.

content.concept: Adequate contrast improves readability and helps users distinguish text and interface elements.
content.tip: Higher contrast generally improves readability, but avoid using contrast alone to communicate meaning.
